plan: This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with 3 bidders and independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy — it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks winning at a loss; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $28.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid one's true value, regardless of beliefs about others' bids. Bidding above value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $23, bidding exactly $23 maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win whenever profitable and pay only the second-highest bid, which is optimal regardless of competitors' strategies.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others bid. This is because you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win, so there's no incentive to shade your bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value of $36 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the highest competing bid (profitable), and lose when it doesn't (avoiding a loss). This maximizes expected profit.
